hierarchy_note: Higher entries win. CMS-4201-F: MA plans may not apply internal criteria or MCG more restrictively than Traditional Medicare NCD/LCD/regulation.
covered_cpt_note: The curated criteria apply ONLY to the procedures listed under `procedures`. Any other CPT has no entry here: the engine refuses to score it against another service's criteria and routes it to the retrieval fallback (pipeline/policy_retrieval.py), whose output a person must confirm.

questions.asks: Is inpatient the right level of care (vs outpatient or observation)?
Is the procedure itself covered and medically necessary for this patient?

criteria.text: Admitting physician expects the patient to need hospital care crossing at least 2 midnights.
criteria.if_missing: Ask: how many midnights does the surgeon expect the patient to need hospital care?
criteria.short: the expected stay does not cross 2 midnights

criteria.text: The factors behind that expectation are documented in the record (history and comorbidities, severity of signs and symptoms, current medical needs, risk of an adverse event).
criteria.if_missing: Ask: which comorbidities or risk factors support the expected stay?

criteria.text: Exception: a stay under 2 midnights can still be inpatient on the admitting physician's documented clinical judgment.

policies.title: Lumbar Spinal Fusion
policies.source: CMS Medicare Coverage Database, LCD L37848 v18, Palmetto GBA (MAC Part A and B), effective 09/12/2024
policies.applies_to: CPT 22612 and other lumbar fusion, within the Palmetto GBA jurisdiction. LCDs are jurisdiction-specific; the policy table must key by MAC jurisdiction.

criteria.text: Documentation shows the patient meets at least 1 indication: (1) radiographic or clinical evidence of instability (e.g. chronic degenerative conditions), (2) symptomatic spinal deformity meeting criteria, (3) revision for pseudarthrosis meeting criteria, (4) symptomatic neural compression needing disc excision.
criteria.if_missing: Ask: what imaging or clinical findings document instability, deformity, pseudarthrosis or neural compression at each level to be fused?

criteria.text: The record reflects which conservative treatments were tried or why the patient is not a candidate (medical therapy, physical and exercise therapy, injections).
criteria.if_missing: Ask: which conservative treatments were tried, and for how long?

criteria.text: Where possible, shared decision making with the patient is documented, including risks and benefits.
criteria.if_missing: Ask: is shared decision making documented?

criteria.text: If more than 1 level is fused, the record shows each fused level is affected by a qualifying condition.

policies.title: Inpatient level of care for elective spinal surgery (ILLUSTRATIVE)
policies.source: Humana Use Case 1 brief, sample medical policy. Made up for the exercise. Not a real Humana policy.

criteria.text: Documented comorbidities that raise peri-operative risk (for example heart failure, COPD, uncontrolled diabetes).
criteria.if_missing: Ask: which comorbidities raise peri-operative risk?

criteria.text: Post-operative monitoring or care needs that cannot be safely provided in an outpatient or observation setting.
criteria.if_missing: Ask: what post-operative monitoring or care needs cannot be met outside the hospital?
criteria.short: no post-operative needs beyond routine recovery are documented

policies.title: Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillators (ICDs)
policies.source: CMS Medicare Coverage Database, NCD 20.4 v5, effective 07/31/2023 (last reviewed February 2018)
policies.verified_from: CMS Coverage database download (policies/corpus/ncds.json), source text saved in policies/raw/NCD_20_4.txt
policies.applies_to: Primary prevention for ischemic or non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (NCD 20.4, B3 and B4). Other covered pathways (B1, B2, B5) are not modeled and go to a physician.

criteria.text: The request rests on ischemic or non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy with heart failure. The other covered pathways (prior sustained ventricular tachycardia or cardiac arrest, prior heart attack with LVEF 30% or less, inherited rhythm disorders) are outside this prototype and go to a physician.
criteria.if_missing: Ask: what is the cause of the cardiomyopathy: ischemic (coronary disease or prior heart attack) or non-ischemic?
criteria.short: the indication is a pathway this prototype does not model

criteria.text: Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 35% or less.
criteria.if_missing: Ask: what is the most recent ejection fraction, how was it measured, and on what date?

criteria.text: LVEF was measured by echocardiography, nuclear imaging, cardiac MRI, or catheter angiography.
criteria.if_missing: Ask: how was the ejection fraction measured?
criteria.short: the ejection fraction was not measured by an accepted method

criteria.text: Heart failure is NYHA class II or III.
criteria.if_missing: Ask: what is the patient's NYHA heart failure class?
criteria.short: the NYHA class is not II or III

criteria.text: No heart attack in the past 40 days, and no bypass surgery or stent procedure in the past 3 months.
criteria.if_missing: Ask: has the patient had a heart attack in the past 40 days, or bypass surgery or a stent in the past 3 months?
criteria.short: there was a recent heart attack, bypass, or stent

criteria.text: For non-ischemic cardiomyopathy: the patient has been on optimal medical therapy for at least 3 months.
criteria.if_missing: Ask: how long has the patient been on optimal heart failure medicines?
criteria.short: the patient has had under 3 months of optimal medical therapy

criteria.text: A formal shared decision making visit, using an evidence-based decision tool, took place before the implant.
criteria.if_missing: Ask: is a shared decision making visit with a decision tool documented before the implant?
criteria.short: no shared decision making visit is documented

criteria.text: The patient is clinically stable and has no condition that rules out an ICD (severe brain damage, another illness with survival under 1 year, poorly controlled atrial fibrillation).
criteria.if_missing: Ask: is the patient clinically stable, and are there any conditions that limit survival or rule out an ICD?
criteria.short: a condition that rules out an ICD is documented

policies.title: Bariatric Surgery for Treatment of Co-Morbid Conditions Related to Morbid Obesity
policies.source: CMS Medicare Coverage Database, NCD 100.1 v5, effective 09/24/2013
policies.verified_from: CMS Coverage database download (policies/corpus/ncds.json), source text saved in policies/raw/NCD_100_1.txt
policies.applies_to: Open and laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (CPT 43644), nationally covered. Stand-alone sleeve gastrectomy is decided by each Medicare contractor and is not modeled.

criteria.text: Body-mass index (BMI) is 35 or higher.
criteria.if_missing: Ask: what is the patient's BMI, and when was it measured?

criteria.text: At least one comorbidity related to obesity is documented (type 2 diabetes counts).
criteria.if_missing: Ask: which obesity-related conditions does the patient have, such as type 2 diabetes?

criteria.text: The patient was previously unsuccessful with medical treatment for obesity.
criteria.if_missing: Ask: what medical treatment for obesity was tried, for how long, and what was the result?
criteria.short: no unsuccessful medical treatment is documented

open_items: Confirm whether CPT 22612 is on the CMS inpatient-only list (OPPS Addendum E). Not verified; the inpatient-only list is a payment-rule list, not an LCD.
Confirm which MAC jurisdictions cover the member's state and whether other MACs publish their own lumbar fusion LCD.
Check for an NCD that touches lumbar fusion beyond NCD 150.10 (artificial disc). Index search found none for fusion.
ICD: only the primary-prevention cardiomyopathy pathways (NCD 20.4 B3 and B4) are modeled. Secondary prevention, prior MI with LVEF 30% or less, and inherited disorders route to a physician.
Bariatric: Roux-en-Y bypass is nationally covered. Stand-alone sleeve gastrectomy is decided by each Medicare contractor, so it is not modeled.
The new criteria were written from the NCD text and have not been signed off by a clinical policy owner.

facts.label: Expected stay
facts.ask: Number of midnights of hospital care the physician expects. If the text only says something like 'a multi-day stay' with no number, use status implied.

facts.label: Comorbidities
facts.ask: Short labels for the patient's conditions that raise risk, for example 'heart failure'. Use status none only when the packet says there are none.

facts.label: Post-op care needs
facts.ask: Post-operative monitoring or care needs. Use status none only if the packet says recovery is routine.
facts.hint: What care is needed after surgery

facts.label: Surgical indication
facts.phrase: imaging or exam evidence for the surgical indication
facts.ask: The qualifying finding on imaging or exam. Use status none when the imaging or exam explicitly RULES OUT a finding (for example 'no evidence of instability'). That is not the same as missing.

facts.label: Conservative care
facts.ask: Which non-surgical treatments were tried and for how long (therapy, medicines, injections).
facts.hint: What was tried and for how long

facts.label: Shared decision making
facts.ask: A documented shared decision making discussion with the patient, including risks and benefits.

facts.label: Expected stay
facts.ask: Number of midnights of hospital care the physician expects. If the text only says something like 'a multi-day stay' with no number, use status implied.

facts.label: Comorbidities
facts.ask: Short labels for the patient's conditions that raise risk, for example 'heart failure'. Use status none only when the packet says there are none.

facts.label: Ejection fraction
facts.ask: The most recent measured left ventricular ejection fraction, as a percent number. If two measurements conflict, use the later one and say so in the note.

facts.label: How it was measured
facts.phrase: how the ejection fraction was measured
facts.ask: How the most recent ejection fraction was measured.

facts.label: NYHA class
facts.ask: The New York Heart Association functional class of heart failure, I to IV.

facts.label: Cause of heart failure
facts.ask: ischemic if caused by coronary artery disease or a prior heart attack. non-ischemic if dilated cardiomyopathy without a coronary cause. other if the request rests on something else, such as prior sustained ventricular tachycardia, cardiac arrest, or an inherited rhythm disorder.

facts.label: Recent heart attack, bypass, or stent
facts.phrase: whether there was a heart attack in the past 40 days or a bypass or stent in the past 3 months
facts.ask: Use status found if a heart attack within 40 days, or bypass surgery or a stent within 3 months, is documented. Use status none only if the packet states there was none, or gives dates that are outside those windows.

facts.label: Months on heart failure medicines
facts.phrase: how long the patient has been on optimal heart failure medicines
facts.ask: Number of months on guideline-directed heart failure medical therapy.

facts.label: Shared decision making
facts.ask: A documented formal shared decision making visit between the patient and a physician or qualified practitioner, using an evidence-based decision tool on ICDs, before the implant.

facts.label: Conditions that rule out an ICD
facts.phrase: whether any condition rules out an ICD
facts.ask: Conditions that rule out an ICD: severe irreversible brain damage, a non-cardiac illness with expected survival under 1 year, atrial fibrillation with a poorly controlled rate, or a patient who is not clinically stable. Use status none only if the packet says there are none.
facts.hint: For example: none, or the condition
